artists.biography: Justin Townes Earle (born January 4, 1982) is an American singer-songwriter and musician. Earle records with Bloodshot Records and has five released albums from 2007–2012. He is the son of alternative country artist, Steve Earle.  Earle grew up in South Nashville, Tennessee, with his mother, Carol Ann Hunter Earle. His father Steve Earle gave Justin his middle name in honor of his mentor Townes van Zandt, but left Justin's mother when he was 2.

perplexity.description:
Midnight at the Movies, released in 2009 on Bloodshot Records, is the second studio album by Justin Townes Earle and a defining work in his early career. The album blends traditional folk, country, and Americana, showcasing Earle’s sharp songwriting and roots-oriented sound. With its warm acoustic textures, pedal steel, fiddle, and subtle touches of blues and rock, the record evokes a timeless, rural atmosphere. Standout tracks like “Mama’s Eyes” and “They Killed John Henry” highlight Earle’s ability to weave narrative storytelling with emotional depth, while his cover of Paul Westerberg’s “Can’t Hardly Wait” demonstrates his eclectic influences and interpretive skill.

Musically, Midnight at the Movies solidified Earle’s reputation as a leading voice in the alt-country and Americana scenes. It followed his well-received debut, Yuma, and further established his signature style—raw, honest, and deeply rooted in American musical traditions. The album was praised by critics for its authenticity, concise songcraft, and Earle’s distinctive vocals. Though not a major commercial breakthrough, it earned strong reviews and helped build a loyal following, marking a pivotal moment in his discography as he began to carve out his own identity apart from his famous family legacy.
